Furniture Detection vocabulary — what translates differently

Magnifier Detection Mode marketing on App Store pages uses vocabulary general accessibility guides rarely cover. zh-Hans copy should reflect how Chinese buyers describe indoor object detection — not a literal paste of US marketing:

Furniture Detection vs generic object detection

US pages use "Furniture Detection", "Detect furniture", or "Object detection in Magnifier." China storefront copy often uses 家具检测, 检测家具, or 家具识别 — depending on whether you mean Apple's Magnifier Furniture Detection tile, a companion app's indoor awareness story, or general object recognition. AppLocale aligns phrasing with your actual Detection Mode scope, not inventing door, people, or text-reading modes your gallery does not show.

Detection Mode vs close-up zoom

Magnifier hosts both close-up reading zoom and Detection Mode categories. Screenshot galleries often label one or the other. zh-Hans overlay lines should use 家具检测 or 检测模式 vocabulary for furniture-outline frames — not 放大镜 or 阅读放大 unless that frame shows reading zoom, not Detection Mode.
